Subject: Post-call: Embedding fit validation for Silverleaf search demo

Hi Evelyn / Liam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick internal/external recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

What we heard (use case summary)
- Primary: site product search across editorial + commerce catalogs (12M documents, avg ~250 tokens).
- Secondary: related-items recommendations and a short-form personalization signal for editorial surfacing.
- Data: mix of English + French; 20% of items have long-form descriptions (>1k tokens); frequent catalog churn (daily).
- Success metrics you called out: improve search MRR/nDCG over current BM25 baseline, and reduce manual triage by 40%. 99th pct latency target for query path: ~150ms.

Initial embedding fit assessment (high level)
- Dimensionality: recommend 384–768 dims as starting points. Higher dims (1024+) may help recall for long documents but add cost and index size.
- Candidate models to benchmark: sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 (baseline), sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (lower-cost), and redwood-embed-large (higher-quality — Redwood hosted).
- Similarity metric: cosine for dense, with hybrid sparse (+BM25) option for tail queries. We should test recall@10, MRR, nDCG@10, and AUC for rerank tasks.
- Drift and stability: run temporal-split evaluations (most recent 3 months as holdout) and compute mean cosine shift and silhouette scores by cohort to detect embedding drift.

Quality/regression concerns
- Long-document chunking: need consistent chunk size and pooling strategy (max, mean, first-k). We'll include both chunked and whole-doc evals.
- Multilingual handling: run per-language slices (EN vs FR) to ensure no regression in FR.
- Indexing effects: approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) params will affect recall/latency tradeoffs — capture p95/p99 query latency for each index config.

Proposed evaluation plan (POC scope)
1) Data sampler: Redwood will run a stratified sampler (3k labeled queries + 10k unlabeled doc samples). You can also provide your own QA pairs if available.
2) Baseline runs: evaluate 3 candidate models at two index configurations (recall-optimized vs latency-optimized).
3) Metrics dashboard: nDCG@10, MRR, recall@10, P95/P99 latency, index size, storage cost estimate.
4) Drift checks: compute cosine-centroid shift and PCA variance-explained across monthly cohorts.
5) Deliverable: short report + example prompt sets and recommended quantization/indexing config.

Next steps / owners
- Marissa: owner for data ingestion + labeling instructions (action: we need the 3k query sample and a 2-week export of recent docs).
- Ben: owner for procurement/POC capacity and pricing (action: draft hosting vs dedicated cost estimate).
- Karthik (me): owner for model selection and eval harness.

Attachments: embedding-benchmarks-20260620.csv (sample outputs from our internal baseline), prompt-sets-v2.zip (initial prompt set and labeling instructions), sample-docs-10k.jsonl (sample doc export).

Proposed timeline
- Data handoff: by 2026-06-24
- First benchmark run: 2026-06-30
- Review call with results: week of 2026-07-06

Evelyn/Liam — can you confirm the data access mechanism (S3 vs drive share) and whether you have any existing labeled pairs we should include in the 3k sample?

Best,
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — this is super helpful. A few quick clarifications from our end: 

- Data access: S3 (we can provide a short-term role) — I'll confirm the bucket and a read-only role by EOD Wednesday (2026-06-23).
- Labeled pairs: we have ~650 click-derived relevance pairs from the last quarter; happy to share as seed labels.
- Latency: 150ms p99 is an aspirational goal for interactive search; open to a p95 SLA for initial POC.
- Hybrid search: yes we'd like to evaluate a hybrid sparse+dense approach for tail queries — can Redwood run BM25 + dense rerank in the POC?

Also, can you confirm whether the hosted redwood-embed-large model supports FR well or whether you'd recommend a separate FR-tuned model?

Appreciate the timeline — plan looks good. Please include a cost ballpark for 1M queries/month (both hosted and dedicated) in the next note.

Evelyn — thanks, this aligns. Two commercial notes: 

1) Cost framing: for 1M queries/month with a mid-sized embedding (384d) on hosted capacity, expect ~ $1,200–$1,800/month for tokens + compute (ballpark). Dedicated reserved capacity for steady load is likely cheaper long-term but has a setup/commit. I'll follow up with a range and a simple TCO comparison by Wednesday.

2) POC scope: recommend we start on hosted with a small dedicated test pool (24–48 hour window) to measure p95/p99 latency under representative traffic — helps avoid committing to a full dedicated cluster upfront.

On contracts: we'll need an internal DPA + SOC2 attestation for any dedicated/private option; legal should be aware once we move to procurement.
